findings.reason: §1's alt done-when must cover the pre-existing single-unit limitation in `_render_wall_alt`, or the worker will add a vessel line while the alt figure still shows one limiter unit.
findings.text: the plan claims in §1 that the `WallOutline` component dispatch makes "geometry_figure_mpl and equilibrium_chart_alt both show the vessel", but `_render_wall_alt` plots only `wall.wall_r`/`wall.wall_z` and never loops `wall.wall_units`, so the alt backend already drops every limiter unit past the first and has no multi-unit path for a new vessel loop to join (the mpl twin does loop, at imas_ink/mpl.py:368); §1's doubt-when asserts `_render_wall_alt` emits a mark for the shells without noting that the alt wall path itself must first be given the unit loop

findings.reason: §3 must either declare `trace_color` as an addition and state that it changes the default trace colour, or drop the colour clause; as written the done-when cannot be implemented against the current `InkStyle`.
findings.text: §3 says `_render_timeseries_mpl`/`_render_timeseries_alt` apply `trace_linestyle` "together with the style's trace colour" and its done-when asserts both lines are "in the style's trace colour", but `InkStyle` has no trace colour at all (imas_ink/style.py:159-160 defines only `trace_linewidth` and `trace_markersize`; `_render_timeseries_mpl` at imas_ink/mpl.py:540 and `_render_timeseries_alt` at imas_ink/alt.py:350 pass no colour and so use matplotlib's cycle / Altair's default), so the plan silently depends on a second, undeclared public style constant and on changing the default colour of every existing trace figure

findings.reason: an added style default is additive and low-risk beside §3's harder gap; the omission is a completeness point, not one that alters the design.
findings.text: §2 adds `InkStyle.wall_linestyle` and §3 adds `InkStyle.trace_linestyle` without stating, in either section's text, what each retires or merges or why nothing can be, while §1 sets the standard it does not follow ("the field retires nothing; it is the one public addition")

interface_budget-1.reason: plan v4 §3 adds trace_color (ink black) beside trace_linestyle, states today's renderers pass no colour, and asserts both lines in trace_color

interface_budget-2.reason: plan v4 §2 and §3 state that wall_linestyle, trace_color and trace_linestyle retire nothing because no style field sets those today

reuse_search-1.reason: plan v4 §1: _render_wall_alt first gains the wall_units loop the matplotlib renderer has, and the vessel shells join that loop in both backends; the done-when asserts a mark per limiter unit and per shell

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan deepens three existing functions (`extract_vessel_shells` gains outline-pair reading, `geometry_figure_mpl` gains an `ax` target, `time_trace_figure_mpl` gains a multi-series panel) rather than spreading new shallow wrappers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — §1 extends `extract_vessel_shells` (`imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:151`) instead of forking a second vessel extractor, reuses the already-exported `VesselShell` type, and reuses `_select_description_2d` (`imas_ink/extract.py:322`) as the selection owner; no placement, path-resolution, scheduler or state-reader duplicate is introduced.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 draws on a style "trace colour" that does not exist in `InkStyle` and its done-when depends on it, and §2/§3 add `InkStyle` constants without naming what they retire or why nothing can be, whereas §1 does state that its new field retires nothing.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan extends the existing owners correctly and cites them (it names `extract_vessel_shells`, `_select_description_2d`, `WallOutline`, `geometry_figure_mpl`, `time_trace_figure_mpl`, `ref_lcfs_linestyle`), but its claim that the `WallOutline` component route covers "2D geometry" holds only for the matplotlib backend: `_render_wall_alt` never iterates `WallOutline.wall_units`, so the alt twin of the wall renderer lacks the multi-unit path the mpl one has.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — no new wrapper module is proposed; the `ax=` argument and the single-`TimeSeries`-or-list panel are ordinary extensions of the existing builders, and §1 states explicitly that it extends the one extractor rather than adding a second.
